readerTitle: Your cost per customer doubled. Now what?
caseNote: 가상 시뮬레이션 (포장재 제조사의 검색 광고) · 모든 수치는 설명용
insight: 고객 확보 비용이 올랐을 때는 평균이 아니라 마지막에 쓴 돈이 데려온 고객의 비용을 보고, 그것을 고객이 남기는 돈과 비교한다.
misconception: 고객당 비용이 두 배가 됐으면 광고 전체가 나빠진 것이니 예산을 통째로 줄여야 한다.

sources.text: 마케팅·관리회계의 표준 개념 (고객 확보 비용, 한계 비용, 고객 생애 가치, 홀드아웃 테스트)

cards.title: Your cost per customer doubled. Now what?
body: You run Hollis, a small factory making insulated shipping boxes for bakeries and meal-kit makers. Most new customers find you through search ads.
Last spring, each new customer cost about $120 in ads. This quarter, the number is $240. Your co-owner wants to slash the ad budget today.

image.label: A factory desk with a report showing $120 crossed out and $240 circled
image.brief: 작은 포장재 공장 사무실 책상. 단열 박스가 쌓여 있고, 보고서에 "$120"이 줄 그어지고 "$240"이 빨간 원으로 표시됨. 실제 광고 플랫폼 로고는 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: What's your first move?
body: Ad spend rose from $6,000 to $12,000 a month over the year. New customers stayed at about 50 a month.

options.text: Cut the ad budget in half right away
options.feedback: Costs drop fast, but you may cut your cheapest customers along with the expensive ones. You'd be acting before knowing where the money is leaking.

options.text: Split the spending into slices and see what each slice brings in
options.feedback: It takes a few days, but it shows whether all the spending got worse or only part of it.

options.text: Raise your bids to win back more clicks
options.feedback: More volume, maybe, but at an even higher price per customer, before you know why it rose.

cards.title: The average was hiding two different stories.
body: Rivals now bid on the same keywords, so the first slice got pricier. But the real problem is the second slice. Each extra customer there cost **$600**. The $240 average blended a fair deal with a bad one.
cards.softwareNote: An app sees the same thing when cost per signup doubles. The cheapest audiences get used up first, so the last dollars buy the priciest users.

cards.title: Which slices are worth paying for?
body: Customers reorder. In their first year, a typical customer leaves about $400 after box and shipping costs.

options.text: Cut any spending above the old $120 benchmark
options.feedback: Safe, but $120 was last year's price, not a limit. At $150, each customer still leaves $250.

options.text: Keep the first slice, cut the extra $6,000
options.feedback: The first slice earns about $250 per customer. The extra slice loses about $200 on each one. You keep the profit and save $6,000 a month.

options.text: Stop all ads, since a first order barely covers $150
options.feedback: Judging by the first order ignores the reorders. You'd give up 40 profitable customers a month.

cards.title: You have $6,000 a month back. Where does it go?

options.text: Move it all to a new ad platform
options.feedback: Untested channels can be cheap at first, but you'd bet the full amount before seeing a single result.

options.text: Test a new channel small, and fund referrals and packing guides for food makers
options.feedback: Small tests limit the downside. Referrals and guides keep bringing customers after you stop paying for them.
Profit improves now, but growth stalls if the remaining ad slice gets pricier.

cards.title: Your cheapest ads look almost too good.
body: Three months on, ads on searches for your own name cost $1,000 a month and bring 25 customers: $40 each. Many of these people already knew you.

options.text: Spend more on them. $40 is your best deal
options.feedback: Maybe. But if these buyers would have found you anyway, the real cost per extra customer is much higher.

options.text: Pause them in a few regions for a month and compare
options.feedback: A small test shows how many sales the ads actually cause, for little risk.
You save $1,000, but a rival could start winning searches for your name.

cards.title: These numbers are estimates, not facts.
body: Ten customers is a small sample. One slow month can make a slice look twice as costly. Check a few months before cutting.
The $400 customer value is a forecast. If reorders fall, every slice gets worse. And costs move with seasons and rivals, so the right budget this quarter may be wrong next quarter.

cards.title: Ask what your last dollar bought, and what that customer is worth.
body: Each decision used one idea from this unit:
list: **Split the spending:** diminishing returns hide inside averages
**Compare to customer value:** paying for customers only works if they leave more than they cost
**Fund referrals and guides:** organic growth keeps working after you stop paying
**Pause and compare:** check whether marketing caused the sale
cards.callout: **Try it today:** split last month's ad spend into two halves and estimate the customers each half brought in.
